STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r27.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r27.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r27.claim: The discussion returns to the Israelites' later disobedience and the future punishments they are said to suffer for it.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r27.anchor: the Israelites’ later disobedience and the future punishments they are said to suffer as a result (vv. 159–71)

NAHHAS:v2p160/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p160/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p160/r2.claim: The phrase wa-minhum dūna dhālika is a nominal sentence, with dūna in the adverbial accusative; the author knows no one who reads it nominatively.
NAHHAS:v2p160/r2.anchor: رفع بالابتداء ( ومنهم دون ذلك ) منصوب على الظرف ولا نعلم أحدا رفعه

STUDYQURAN:7:168/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r1.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r1.claim: The Israelites' division into communities around the earth is understood as the Jewish Diaspora.
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r1.anchor: taken as a reference to the Diaspora, the existence of smaller communities of Jews in various locations throughout the world

STUDYQURAN:7:168/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r2.claim: Righteousness remains possible for Jews who follow the Law and ritual prescribed in the Torah, including Sabbath observance emphasized by the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r2.anchor: a life of righteousness continues to be possible for those who follow Jewish Law and ritual as prescribed in the Torah

STUDYQURAN:7:168/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r3.claim: Those described as otherwise are members of the Jewish community who do not follow the law.
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r3.anchor: those who do not follow the law, although they continue to be members of this community

STUDYQURAN:7:168/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r4.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r4.claim: Many commentators take the righteous Jews to mean Jews of the past, before Muhammad or even before Jesus.
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r4.anchor: to pertain to the Jewish community of the past, before the coming of the Prophet Muhammad or even before the coming of Jesus

STUDYQURAN:7:168/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r5.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r5.claim: Another interpretation identifies the righteous Jews as those in Madinah who became Muslim.
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r5.anchor: or else to the Jews in Madinah who became Muslim (R)

STUDYQURAN:7:168/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r6.claim: The author questions those readings: the present tense points to the present and indefinite future, and to Jews who remain Jews.
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r6.anchor: the verse is clearly in the present tense, indicating that it pertains to the present and the indefinite future

STUDYQURAN:7:168/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r7.claim: Good things are worldly provision and ease; evil things are forms of worldly adversity.
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r7.anchor: The good things with which God tries them include worldly provision and ease; the evil things are various forms of worldly adversity

STUDYQURAN:7:168/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r8.claim: Trials through good and bad fortune apply generally, not only to Jews, as 21:35 says explicitly.
STUDYQURAN:7:168/r8.anchor: The trial by both good and bad fortune is not particular to the Jewish population, but is meant in a more general sense

TAB-FULL:v10p534/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r1.claim: God dispersed the Children of Israel through the lands as separate groups.

TAB-FULL:v10p534/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says that every land entered by a people had a group of Jews in it.
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r2.anchor: في كل أرض يدخلها قوم من اليهود

TAB-FULL:v10p534/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r3.claim: Mujāhid identifies the dispersed groups as Jews.
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد

TAB-FULL:v10p534/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r4.claim: Among the Israelites, some were righteous, meaning believers in God and His messengers, while others fell below that standard.

TAB-FULL:v10p534/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r5.claim: This description applied before they turned back from their religion and disbelieved, before Jesus son of Mary was sent among them.
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r5.anchor: قبل ارتدادهم عن دينهم وقبل كفرهم

TAB-FULL:v10p534/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r6.claim: The good things are prosperity, comfort, ease, and abundance of provision; the bad things are hardship, austere living, calamities, and losses of wealth.
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r6.anchor: وهي الحسنات التي ذكرها جل ثناؤه

TAB-FULL:v10p534/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p534/r7.claim: God tested them so that they would return to obedience, turn back to Him, and repent of their sins.

TABATABAI:7:167-169/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:167-169/r5.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:7:167-169/r5.claim: Al-Majma' says dun in 'some of them below that' is nominative as the subject, but appears accusative because it is established as an adverbial; likewise bayn in 'the bond between you is severed,' and in 'He will decide between you' it is nominative as deputy subject.
TABATABAI:7:167-169/r5.anchor: قال في المجمع دون في موضع الرفع بالابتداء

TABATABAI:7:167-169/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:167-169/r6.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:7:167-169/r6.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means 'among them is a group below that'; the noun 'group' is omitted and its adjective stands in its place.
TABATABAI:7:167-169/r6.anchor: وإن شئت كان التقدير ومنهم جماعة دون ذلك فحذف الموصوف وقامت صفته مقامه

TABATABAI:7:167-169/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:167-169/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:167-169/r7.claim: The good and bad things with which God tested them are the blessings and afflictions of worldly life.
TABATABAI:7:167-169/r7.anchor: والمراد بالحسنات والسيئات نعماء الدنيا وضراءها

TABRISI:7:167-168/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:167-168/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:167-168/r7.claim: Duna dhalika is grammatically nominative as a subject but appears accusative because of its adverbial force; another analysis supplies an omitted “group” and treats the phrase as its adjective.
TABRISI:7:167-168/r7.anchor: ومنهم دون ذلك دون في موضع الرفع بالابتداء ولكنه جاء منصوبا لتمكنه في الظرفية

TABRISI:7:167-168/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:167-168/r8.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:7:167-168/r8.claim: Abu al-Hasan compares the adverbial accusative construction with “Your ties have been cut off” and “on the Day of Resurrection He will distinguish between you.”
TABRISI:7:167-168/r8.anchor: على قول أبي الحسن لقد تقطع بينكم وهو في موضع الرفع فجاء منصوبا لهذا المعنى وكذلك

TABRISI:7:167-168/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:167-168/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:167-168/r9.claim: Alternatively, an implied noun “group” is omitted: “among them is a group below that,” with the adjective standing in its place.
TABRISI:7:167-168/r9.anchor: وإن شئت كان التقدير ومنهم جماعة دون ذلك فحذف الموصوف وقامت صفته مقامه

TABRISI:7:167-168/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:167-168/r12.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
TABRISI:7:167-168/r12.claim: The scattered groups are the Jews, dispersed among different lands and divided into varied communities.
TABRISI:7:167-168/r12.anchor: وفرقناهم في البلاد فرقا مختلفة وجماعات شتى يعني اليهود عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

TABRISI:7:167-168/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:167-168/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:167-168/r13.claim: God divided their inclinations, causing them to disperse; this weakened their mutual support and humiliated them like the taking of jizya.
TABRISI:7:167-168/r13.anchor: بأن فرق دواعيهم حتى افترقوا في البلاد وتفرقهم ذل لهم بمنزلة أخذ الجزية لأنهم لا يتعاونون

TABRISI:7:167-168/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:167-168/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:167-168/r14.claim: Another explanation is that God divided them for their religious welfare, so one group became righteous while another disobeyed.
TABRISI:7:167-168/r14.anchor: وقيل: إنه فرقهم لما علم سبحانه من الصلاح

TABRISI:7:167-168/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:167-168/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:167-168/r15.claim: The righteous among the Israelites are those who believe in God and His messengers and obey Him.
TABRISI:7:167-168/r15.anchor: أي من هؤلاء الصالحون يعني من بني إسرائيل وهم الذين يؤمنون بالله ورسله ويطيعونه

TABRISI:7:167-168/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:167-168/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:167-168/r16.claim: Those below the righteous in rank obeyed some commands, disobeyed others, and committed some sins; this describes their condition before their later apostasy, before Jesus was sent.
TABRISI:7:167-168/r16.anchor: دون الصالح في الدرجة والمنزلة وهم الذين امتثلوا بعض الأوامر دون بعض وعملوا بعض المعاصي

TABRISI:7:167-168/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:167-168/r17.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد
TABRISI:7:167-168/r17.claim: A second interpretation takes the righteous as believers in Muhammad and Jesus, and the others as disbelievers.
TABRISI:7:167-168/r17.anchor: وقيل: معناه منهم المؤمنون بمحمد وعيسى ع ومنهم الكافرون عن عطاء ومجاهد

TABRISI:7:167-168/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:167-168/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:167-168/r18.claim: The tests were prosperity, worldly ease, abundance, and comfort, as well as hardship and calamities affecting lives and property; blessings prompt people to seek their continuance from God, while afflictions prompt them to ask relief.
TABRISI:7:167-168/r18.anchor: اختبرناهم بالرخاء في العيش والخفض في الدنيا والدعة والسعة في الرزق وبالشدائد في العيش والمصائب

TABRISI:7:167-168/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:167-168/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:167-168/r19.claim: The tests are meant to bring them back to God, obedience, and compliance with His command.
TABRISI:7:167-168/r19.anchor: أي لكي يرجعوا إلى الله تعالى وينيبوا إلى طاعته وامتثال أمره

TABRISI:7:167-168/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:167-168/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:167-168/r20.claim: Although they may not have previously followed the command, “return” can mean to turn toward something; it resembles telling someone in danger to return to the straight path, or it can mean returning to their original innate disposition.
TABRISI:7:167-168/r20.anchor: فالقول فيه أن الذاهب عن الشيء قد يقال له أرجع إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God dispersed them throughout the lands.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: فرقناهم في جميع البلاد)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r2.claim: The people of meaning say God scattered them so their affairs fell apart and they no longer shared a united word.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r2.anchor: قال أهل المعاني (¬6): (فرقهم الله تعالى فتشتت أمرهم، ولم تجتمع لهم كلمة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the righteous as those who met the Prophet and believed in him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1) ومجاهد (¬2): (يريد: الذين أدركوا النبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r4.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r4.claim: Mujahid likewise identifies the righteous as those who met and believed in the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1) ومجاهد (¬2): (يريد: الذين أدركوا النبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies them with the community in 7:159 that guides by the truth, which he says lives beyond China.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (يعني: الذين ذكرهم في قوله: {ومن قوم موسى أمة يهدون بالحق}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r6.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says those below that rank are the ones who disbelieved.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ومنهم دون ذلك}، قال: (يريد: الذين كفروا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r7.claim: To test them means to deal with them as one who is testing does.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r7.anchor: وقوله: {وبلوناهم}، أي: عاملناهم معاملة المبتلي المختبر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r8.claim: The good things are blessings, abundance, and well-being; the bad things are droughts and hardships.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r8.anchor: {بالحسنات}، وهي: النعيم والخصب والعافية، {والسيئات} وهي: الجدب والشدائد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r9.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r9.claim: The people of meaning say both blessings and calamities call people to obedience: blessings invite attachment and hope of more, while calamities invite relief and safety.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p426/r9.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: (وكل واحد من الحسنات والسيئات يدعو إلى الطاعة، أما النعم فلارتباطها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses their return as repentance.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428/r2.claim: The people of meaning picture them heading toward falsehood and being called back toward truth; turning away from falsehood is returning to truth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p428/r2.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: (إنهم مارون على وجوههم في جهة الباطل , فدعوا إلى الرجوع عنه إلى جهة الحق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r6.claim: God scattered them among different lands, so they no longer shared a united community.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r6.anchor: فرقناهم في البلاد، فلم يجتمع لهم كلمة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r7.claim: The righteous are those who believed; the others are those who disbelieved.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r7.anchor: منهم الصالحون } وهم الذين آمنوا { ومنهم دون ذلك } الذين كفروا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r8.claim: Good things mean prosperity and well-being; bad things mean drought and hardships.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r8.anchor: بالحسنات } بالخصب والعافية { والسيئات } الجدب والشدائد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:166-169/r9.claim: These trials were intended to bring them to repentance.

ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r5.claim: Elmalılı renders the phrase as scattering the Israelites across the earth and dividing them into many communities.
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r5.anchor: ve onları, o kavm-i Mûsâ’yı yeryüzünde parça parça ettik, birçok ümmetlere ayırdık.

ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r6.claim: The earlier organization into twelve tribes under Moses preserved national unity and was a blessing; this later dispersion began their decline and ended their collective power.
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r6.anchor: risâlet-i Mûsâ tahtında vahdet-i kavmiyelerini bozmayan bir teşkîlât ve mukaddime-i kemâlleri olan bir nimet idi.

ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r7.claim: After this dispersion they were scattered throughout the earth and could no longer gather strength.
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r7.anchor: Arzın her tarafına perişan bir surette dağıldılar ve artık bir şevket toplayamaz oldular.

ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r8.claim: Some of the dispersed Israelites remained righteous, like the believers in Medina who guided by truth and judged by it; others fell below righteousness at varying levels.
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r8.anchor: içlerinden bazıları ehl-i salâh Medine’de iman edenler gibi bâlâda geçen

ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r9.claim: Israel's state collapsed despite righteous people among them: wicked people were numerous and controlled the community, which represented sin and injustice as a whole.
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r9.anchor: dağılmaları içlerinde iyiler hiç bulunmadığından değil, kötülerin kesretinden ve hey’et-i umûmiyesi kötüler elinde bulunup fısk u zulmü temsil etmesinden idi.

ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r10.claim: God tested the dispersed groups with blessings such as health, wealth, and prosperity and with their opposites; peoples such as the Magi and Romans supplied bitter lessons.
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r10.anchor: hem hasenât -sıhhat ve servet ü refah- hem de bunların zıddı seyyiât ile imtihan ettik.

ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r11.claim: The trials were meant to turn them from disbelief and sin back to truth and righteousness; some repented, but others did not before Muhammad's era.
ELMALILI:7:164-170#2/r11.anchor: rücû‘edeler küfr ü masiyetten tevbe edip hakka döneler, salâha yüz tutalar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r9.claim: Condemning an entire people is irrational and unethical, conflicts with Qur'anic justice, and ignores Israel's hope of mercy in 17:4–8 if they do not return to evil; verses 168–170 affirm justice for Jews and all people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r9.anchor: bir toplumu bu şekilde toptan mahkûm etmek hem aklen ve ahlâken doğru değildir hem de bizzat Kur’an-ı Kerîm’in herkese ve her topluma hak ettiği şekilde muamele edileceğini ve hiçbir kimseye hiçbir şekilde haksızlık yapılmayacağını belirten açıklamalarına

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r10.claim: The verse describes Jews dispersed after losing their homelands because of corruption; like every people, they include good and bad, and the bad are tested with good fortune to encourage return.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r10.anchor: Yahudilerin bozgunculukları sebebiyle yurtlarını kaybederek dünyanın çeşitli yerlerine dağılmışlıklarını ifade eden 168. âyette her topluluk gibi onların da iyilerinin ve kötülerinin bulunduğu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r11.speaker: bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r11.claim: Some exegetes say this verse speaks about Jews in Moses's time.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r11.anchor: Bazı müfessirler burada Hz. Mûsâ dönemi yahudilerinden söz edildiğini ileri sürmüşlerse de

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r12.claim: The author finds the Moses-era identification implausible because dispersion began later; 7:169's opening points to Jewish groups living before Islam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r12.anchor: Zira dağılma süreci Hz. Mûsâ’dan sonra başlamıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r13.speaker: eski müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r13.claim: Most early exegetes identify the righteous as Jews who entered Islam and the others as those who remained Jewish.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r13.anchor: Eski müfessirlerin çoğunluğu, âyetteki “iyi kimseler”den yahudi iken İslâmiyet’e girenlerin, böyle olmayanlarla da Yahudiliğe bağlılığını sürdürenlerin kastedildiğini ileri sürmüşlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r14.claim: The author rejects limiting the verse's meaning to that classification when the Qur'an itself makes no such distinction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r14.anchor: Kur’an böyle bir belirleme yoluna gitmediği halde âyetin anlamını sınırlamanın doğru olmadığı kanaatindeyiz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r15.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r15.claim: Tabari offers a broader sense for the righteous: those who believe in God and the prophets, which the author presents instead of the narrower classification.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r15.anchor: Taberî böyle bir yorum yapmak yerine, “iyi kimseler” meâlindeki kısmı, “Allah’a ve peygamberlere inananlar” şeklinde daha genel bir ifadeyle açıklamıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r16.speaker: Elmalılı
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r16.claim: Elmalılı says Israel's states collapsed and the people dispersed because wicked people were numerous and controlled the polity, not because no righteous people existed; both good and corrupt remained.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r16.anchor: Demek ki Benî İsrâil’in devletleri tarumar olup böyle dağılmaları, içlerinde iyiler hiç bulunmadığından değil, kötülerin kesretinden ve hey’et-i umûmiyyesi kötüler elinde bulunup fısku zulmü temsil etmesinden idi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r17.claim: Every blessing and hardship is a test: gratitude and fulfilling duties in prosperity, and patient, steadfast worship during difficulty, mark success.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r17.anchor: Allah’ın verdiği her nimet ve her sıkıntının bir imtihan olduğu, diğer milletler gibi yahudilerin de böyle denemelere tâbi tutulduğu bildirilmektedir. Nimetin değerini bilip onu verene şükreden

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r18.claim: Viewing blessings and hardships as tests brings both salvation in the afterlife and worldly benefits, especially unity and a sound political and social life in one's homeland.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:167/r18.anchor: nimetleri ve sıkıntıları böyle bir imtihan bilinci ve sorumluluğu ile algılayıp değerlendirmek, insanları sadece âhiret kurtuluşuna götürmekle kalmayacak, dünyevî faydalar da kazandıracak

BURHAN:v4p274/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p274/r5.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v4p274/r5.claim: دون can be a vague spatial adverb in any of six directions or can indicate being below someone in place or rank; Sibawayh defines it as falling short of a limit.
BURHAN:v4p274/r5.anchor: وقال سيبويه واما دون فتقصير عن الغاية قال الصفار لايريد الغاية على الاطلاق

BURHAN:v4p274/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p274/r6.speaker: الصفار
BURHAN:v4p274/r6.claim: Al-Saffar clarifies that Sibawayh means short of the next limit specifically; being دون someone in knowledge means occupying a lower position by metaphor.
BURHAN:v4p274/r6.anchor: قال الصفار لايريد الغاية على الاطلاق بل الغاية التي تكون بعدها فاذا قلت انا دونك في العلم

BURHAN:v4p274/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p274/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p274/r7.claim: دون can function as a noun or as an adjective meaning bad; it can also modify a noun while retaining its spatial sense, and omitted nouns permit two dialects of inflection.
BURHAN:v4p274/r7.anchor: الثاني اسم نحو ﴿ من دونه ﴾ 1 الثالث صفة نحو هذا الشيء دون أي ردئ

BURHAN:v4p274/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p274/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p274/r8.claim: When the noun modified by دون is omitted, one dialect declines it like a relative and another preserves its adverbial form; ومنهم دون ذلك is read nominative and accusative.
BURHAN:v4p274/r8.anchor: وعليها جاء قوله ﴿ ومنا دون ذلك ﴾ 1 قرئ بالرفع والنصب

SULAMI:v1p247#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p247#3/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p247#3/r1.claim: God tests people with blessings to elicit gratitude and with trials to elicit patience; this group failed at both, showing neither gratitude in ease nor patience in hardship.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r1.claim: The phrase about tearing them apart is metaphorical because tearing properly applies to cloth, yet it remains close to literal since it conveys dispersion; the Qurʾan also says, We scattered them utterly.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r1.anchor: يعد استعارة من حيث إن التمزيق للثوب في أصل اللغة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r2.claim: Cutting a group into communities is a metaphor-like use because cutting properly separates joined things; both senses remove a prior union.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r2.anchor: كان شبه الاستعارة وإن كان المعنى في الموضعين على إزالة الاجتماع ونفيه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r3.claim: Phrases such as interrupting someone's speech or spending time in an activity are a different kind of usage from cutting a dispersed people.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r3.anchor: فإن قلت قطع عليه كلامه أو قلت تقطع الوقت بكذا كان نوعا آخر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r4.claim: To be rich in glory or bankrupt in manliness expresses real abundance or absence, just as one can truly have much knowledge or little understanding; longing and grief work similarly.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r4.anchor: ومن الاستعارة القريبة من الحقيقة قولهم أثرى فلان من المجد وأفلس من المروءة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r5.claim: Calling someone deprived of a liver can be literal: the oddity of bankrupt language applied to nonfinancial needs comes from convention, not from a necessary metaphor.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p44/r5.anchor: لو قلت عدم كبده لم يكن مجازا ولم تجد بينه وبين خلا من كبده وزالت عنه كبده كبير فرق

AKHFASH:v1p341/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p341/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p341/r1.claim: He knows no reader who does not put dūna in the accusative.
AKHFASH:v1p341/r1.anchor: لا نعلم أحدا يقرؤها إلا نصبا

DAMGHANI:v1p191/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r9.anchor: " وبلوناهم بالحسنات والسيئات لعلهم يرجعون " أي يتوبون

DAMGHANI:v1p132/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p132/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p132/r1.claim: In the trial of Israel, good things mean abundant rain and bad things its scarcity; a bad event can mean drought.
DAMGHANI:v1p132/r1.anchor: يعني كثرة المطر وقلته وقال تعالى في سورة الروم

DAMGHANI:v1p385/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p385/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p385/r9.claim: Qaṭṭaʿnāhum means We dispersed them and scattered them across the earth in communities.
DAMGHANI:v1p385/r9.anchor: السادس : القطع هو التفريق والتبديل قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p259/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p259/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p259/r1.claim: A ḥasana is genuinely good without defect; it may also name something containing harm when its good is more apparent, while sayyiʾa is its opposite.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p259/r1.anchor: الحسنة : هي التي لا يشوبها نقص في كونها حسنة . وهذا هو الحقيقة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p259/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p259/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p259/r4.claim: Here ḥasanāt are rain and abundance, while sayyiʾāt are drought and scarcity.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p259/r4.anchor: والثالث : الحسنة : المطر والخصب . والسيئة : قحط المطر والجدب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r1.claim: Qaṭʿ originally means separating things joined together; figurative uses depend on context.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r1.anchor: القطع : في الأصل الفصل بين المتركبين . ثم يستعار في مواضع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r2.claim: Qaṭīʿa means estrangement, qaṭʿ can mean a portion of night, qaṭīʿ a flock, and muqaṭṭaʿāt short garments.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r2.anchor: والقطيعة : الهجران . والقطع : الطائفة من الليل . والقطيع : الطائفة من الغنم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r8.claim: The source labels the usage in this verse as meaning severity or intensity.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p502/r8.anchor: والسادس : الشديد . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p174#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p174#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p174#4/r1.claim: Qattaʿnāhum means that God dispersed them through the land.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p174#4/r1.anchor:
{وقطعناهم في الأرض} أي: فرقناهم.
{وبلوناهم بالحسنات والسيئات} أي: اختبرناهم بالخير والشر والخصب والجدب.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p174#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p174#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p174#4/r2.claim: The tests of good and evil mean prosperity and drought, as well as good and bad fortune.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p174#4/r2.anchor: {وبلوناهم بالحسنات والسيئات} أي: اختبرناهم بالخير والشر والخصب والجدب.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258#2/r2.claim: Both good and bad are called tests: hardship tests patience, while good fortune tests gratitude; fitna here also means testing.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p258#2/r2.anchor: ثم يقال للخير: بلاء، وللشر: بلاء، لأن الاختبار الذي هو بلاء وابتلاء يكون بهما.

MAJAZ:v1p231/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p231/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p231/r3.claim: Qattaʿnāhum fī al-arḍ umaman means We divided them into separate groups.
MAJAZ:v1p231/r3.anchor: «وقطعناهم في الأرض أمما» (167) أي فرقناهم فرقا. «فخلف من بعدهم خلف»

MAJAZ:v1p231/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p231/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p231/r4.claim: Khalaf with a silent second consonant and khalaf with it vocalized can mean the same, like athar and athar. Some distinguish the forms: the first for corrupt successors, the second for good successors.
MAJAZ:v1p231/r4.anchor: «فخلف من بعدهم خلف» (168) ساكن ثانى الحروف، وإن شئت حركت الحرف الثاني وهما فى المعنى واحد

MAJAZ:v1p231/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p231/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p231/r5.claim: ʿAraḍ hādhā al-adnā means the worldly temptation or desire close at hand.
MAJAZ:v1p231/r5.anchor: «عرض هذا الأدنى» (168) أي طمع هذا القريب الذي يعرض لهم فى الدنيا

MAJAZ:v1p231/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p231/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p231/r6.claim: Darasū means they studied the books; darastu imāmī means I memorized and read my teacher’s text, and udurus ʿalā fulān means read to him.
MAJAZ:v1p231/r6.anchor: «ودرسوا ما فيه» (168) مجازه: من دراسة الكتب ويقال: قد درست إمامى أي حفظته وقرأته

SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r1.claim: أمما is either a circumstantial accusative from the object of قطعناهم or a second object, since قطعناهم can carry the sense of صير.
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r1.anchor: إما حال من مفعول " قطعناهم " ، وإما مفعول ثان على ما تقدم من أن قطع

SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows الصالحون to be a بدل from أمم, in addition to the adjective analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r2.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " أو بدل منه، أي: من أمم

SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r3.claim: The phrase has a fronted predicate and an omitted subject such as ناس or قوم; al-Zamakhsharī explains it as people below righteousness, with the descriptive clause standing for its omitted noun.
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r3.anchor: معناه: ومنهم ناس منحطون عن الصلاح، ونحوه:

SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī supports omission of the described noun with 37:164 and the usage منا ظعن ومنا أقام, where a descriptive clause or phrase stands in its place.
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r4.anchor: بمعنى: ما منا أحد إلا له مقام معلوم

SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r5.claim: If الصلاح means faith, Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes دون to mean غير, referring to unbelievers.
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r5.anchor: فإن أريد بالصلاح الإيمان ف " دون " بمعنى " غير " يراد به الكفرة

SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r6.claim: Al-Samīn rejects treating دون as a synonym of غير, while accepting that whoever is below something is necessarily other than it.
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r6.anchor: إن أراد أن " دون " ترادف غيرا فليس بصحيح

SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r7.claim: ذلك may refer to righteousness, requiring an understood أهل for a balanced division, or to the righteous group, which needs no omitted noun.
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r7.anchor: فلا بد من حذف مضاف ليصح المعنى تقديره: ومنهم دون أهل ذلك الصلاح

SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r8.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ calls دون an adverb or predicate, by analogy with 6:94.
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r8.anchor: ودون ذلك ظرف أو خبر على ما ذكرنا في قوله لقد تقطع بينكم

SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r9.claim: Al-Samīn objects to treating دون as a predicate, since دون is not a predicate here.
SAMIN-DURR:7:168/r9.anchor: وفيه نظر من حيث إن " دون " ليس بخبر

ASAD-NOTES:7:167#n134/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:167#n134/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:167#n134/r1.claim: The phrase means that they might return to righteousness.
ASAD-NOTES:7:167#n134/r1.anchor: Lit., "so that they might return [to righteousness]".

NASHR:v1p438/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p438/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p438/r1.claim: For medial hamza, an open hamza after kasra becomes yāʾ when eased, while the other five vowel combinations ease between-between; separated words create nine combinations, including أمما after a kasra in في الأرض أمما.
NASHR:v1p438/r1.anchor: (الثامنة) مضمومة بعد كسر نحو (من كل أمة، في الأرض أمما، في الكتاب أولئك، عليه أمة)

NASHR:v1p491/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p491/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p491/r1.claim: For يشاء إلى, the allowed connected readings are full realization, between-between easing, or pure yāʾ; the same three apply in reverse order to في الأرض أمما.
NASHR:v1p491/r1.anchor: وفيه الثلاثة الجائزة لباقي القراءة وصلا وهي: التحقيق مذهب الجمهور، وبين بين على مذهب أكثر العراقيين، والياء المحضة

NASHR:v1p491/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p491/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p491/r2.claim: The case في الكتاب أولئك has six options: the three preceding treatments plus easing the kasra hamza with either long or short duration.
NASHR:v1p491/r2.anchor: تسهيل الهمزة المكسورة مع المد والقصر

NASHR:v1p491/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p491/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p491/r3.claim: Allowing naql would generate twenty-four further forms across the two mīm-vowel states, but neither state is valid.
NASHR:v1p491/r3.anchor: ولو قرئ بالنقل على مذهب من أجازه لجاء أربعة وعشرون أخرى، وذلك على وجهي فتح الميم وضمها، أي: حالة النقل كما تقدم، وكلاهما لا يصح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p209/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p209/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p209/r16.claim: The Israelites were scattered into separate groups across the earth; every land has some of them, living under humiliation under Muslim or non-Muslim rulers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p209/r16.anchor: أي فرقا متباينين في أقطار الأرض فقل أرض لا يكون منهم فيها شرذمة وهذا حالهم في كل مكان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p209/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p209/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p209/r17.claim: Abū Ḥayyān parses umaman as a circumstantial accusative; al-Ḥawfī instead treats it as a second object, and the author notes an earlier discussion of the phrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p209/r17.anchor: وأمما حال، وقال الحوفي مفعول ثان وتقدم قوله هذا في قطعناهم اثنتي عشرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p209/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p209/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p209/r18.claim: The righteous are variously identified as those who believed in Jesus and Muḥammad or as those who believed in Medina.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p209/r18.anchor: والصالحون من آمن منهم بعيسى ومحمد عليهما السلام أو من آمن بالمدينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r1.claim: If ṣalāḥ means faith, “below that” means unbelievers; if it means worship, goodness, and related traits beyond faith, it can mean believers who have not reached the righteous group’s rank.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r1.anchor: والصالحون ودون ذلك ألفاظ محتملة فإن أريد بالصلاح الإيمان فدون ذلك يراد به الكفار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers the first interpretation, where “below that” means unbelievers, because the tested people are those who remained Jews and left faith, whom God hopes will return.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r2.anchor: والظاهر الاحتمال الأول لقوله لعلهم يرجعون إذ ظاهر قوله وبلوناهم أنهم القوم الذين هم دون أولئك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r3.claim: Dūn is originally a locative adverb and is extended to express lower rank.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says that when righteousness means faith, dūn means “other than,” referring to unbelievers; Abū Ḥayyān rejects treating dūn and ghayr as synonyms but accepts the inference that those below are other than the group.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: فإن أريد بالصلاح الإيمان فدون ذلك بمعنى غير يراد بها الكفرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r5.claim: Dūn is a nominative adverb modifying an omitted noun; alternatively, the described noun is omitted and its quality stands in its place, as in “some of us traveled, some stayed.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r5.anchor: ودون ظرف في موضع رفع نعت لمنعوت محذوف ويجوز في التفصيل بمن حذف الموصوف وإقامة صفته مقامه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r6.claim: The blessings and harms are health, prosperity, and abundance and their opposites.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r6.anchor: أي بالصحة والرخاء والسعة والسيئات مقابلاتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r7.claim: The trials aim to bring them back to obedience and repentance from sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p210/r7.anchor: لعلهم يرجعون إلى الطاعة ويتوبون عن المعصية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r1.claim: God dispersed the Israelites across the earth, placing each group in a region so few regions lacked them; this completed their humiliation and left them without collective strength.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r2.claim: The dispersal is one of the Qurʾān’s reports of the unseen, like the preceding verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r2.anchor: وهذا من مغيبات القرآن كالذي تضمنته الآية قبل

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r3.claim: “Communities” may be the second object of “We dispersed” or a circumstantial accusative describing the dispersed Israelites.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r3.anchor: إما مفعول ثان لقطعنا وإما حال من مفعوله منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r4.claim: “The righteous” may be a subject with a fronted, omitted predicate, or the agent of the adverbial phrase; the clause can describe the communities or function circumstantially.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r4.anchor: والصالحون مبتدأ وجوز أن يكون فاعلا للظرف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r5.speaker: الطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r5.claim: Al-Tabari identifies the righteous as those who believed in God and His Messenger and remained steadfast before Jesus was sent.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r5.anchor: قال الطبري من آمن بالله تعالى ورسوله وثبت على دينه قبل بعث عيسى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid are credited with the view that the righteous were those who lived to meet the Prophet and believed in him.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r6.anchor: هم الذين أدركوا النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وآمنوا به ونسب ذلك إلى ابن عباس ومجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r7.claim: Another view places the righteous Israelites beyond China; al-Ālūsī also locates them there.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r7.anchor: هم الذين وراء الصين وهو عندي وراء الصين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r8.claim: Those below the righteous fall short of their rank: they believe but obey some commands and violate others.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r8.anchor: منحطون عن أولئك الصالحين غير بالغين منزلتهم في الصلاح

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r9.claim: Some take “below that” to mean the Israelites who disbelieved, if “righteousness” here means faith; another view includes both unbelievers and sinners.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r9.anchor: هم الكفرة منهم بناء على أن المراد بالصلاح الإيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r10.speaker: الطبرسي وأبو الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī treats “below” as a subject left in the adverbial form; Abū al-Ḥasan compares its retained fatḥa to “between you” in 6:94.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r10.anchor: على ماذكره الطبرسي مبتدأ إلا أنه بقي مفتوحا لتمكنه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r11.claim: A noun described by an adverb or clause is regularly omitted when it is part of a noun governed by preceding min or fī; an additional proposed parsing is unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r11.anchor: ومن المشهور عند النحاة أن الموصوف بظرف أو جملة يطرد حذفه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r12.claim: The point of the wording is to divide the Israelites into two groups.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r12.anchor: ومحط الفائدة الانقسام إلى أن هؤلاء منقسمون إلى قسمين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r13.claim: The singular demonstrative can refer to the plural righteous; alternatively, it points to righteousness itself, with “people of” understood.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r13.anchor: الإشارة للصالحين وقد ذكروا أن اسم الإشارة الفرد قد يستعمل للمثنى والمجموع

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r14.claim: The good things are fertility and well-being; the bad things are drought and hardship.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r15.claim: The trials are meant to bring them to repent of what they had been forbidden to do.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p95/r15.anchor: أي يتوبون عما كانوا عليه مما نهوا عنه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r1.claim: God divided them into groups, scattering them so their affairs splintered and they could not unite.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r1.anchor: {وقطعناهم} وفرقناهم {في الأرض أمما} فرقا فرقهم الله فتشتت أمرهم ولم تجتمع لهم كلمة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid identify the righteous as those who met the Prophet and believed in him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد: يريد الذين أدركوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وآمنوا به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r3.claim: For Ibn Abbas and Mujahid, the others are those who remained unbelievers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد: يريد الذين أدركوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وآمنوا به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r4.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi places the righteous beyond the river Udaf past China.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: منهم الصالحون هم الذين وراء نهر أوداف من وراء الصين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r5.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies those below that rank as the Jews living on this side.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r5.anchor: ومنهم دون ذلك، يعني: من هاهنا من اليهود،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r6.claim: The good things with which they were tested were prosperity and well-being.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r7.claim: The bad things with which they were tested were drought and hardship.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r8.claim: The tests were intended to turn them back to obedience to their Lord and repentance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p295/r8.anchor: {لعلهم يرجعون} لكي يرجعوا إلى طاعة ربهم ويتوبوا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r1.claim: God dispersed them across the earth in communities, leaving scarcely any region without them, to prevent them regaining collective strength.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r1.anchor: وفرقناهم فيها بحيث لا يكاد يخلو قطر منهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r2.claim: Umaman may be a second object or a circumstantial accusative.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r3.claim: Some are below the righteous in rank: their unbelievers and disobedient members.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r4.claim: The good and bad with which they were tested are blessings and afflictions.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r5.claim: The tests aim to make them stop and turn back from their conduct.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:168-170/r5.anchor: لعلهم يرجعون } ينهون فيرجعون عما كانوا عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r1.claim: He adds the Torah's warnings for Israel's disobedience and injustice to a prior warning in al-Ma'ida about God's curse and wrath.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r1.anchor: ذكر سيء مما هددوا به التوارة على العصيان والبغي والعدوان غير ما تقدم في المائدة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r2.speaker: السفر الخامس
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r2.claim: The fifth book of the Torah warns that failure to keep its commandments and revere God brings painful afflictions upon Israel and its descendants.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r2.anchor: وإن لم تحفظ وتعمل بجميع الوصايا والسنن التي كتبت في هذا الكتاب وتتق الله ربك

BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r3.speaker: السفر الخامس
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r3.claim: The Torah warns that Israel's numerous descendants will dwindle, be driven from their land, live in terror among other peoples, and return toward Egypt to be sold as slaves.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r3.anchor: ويبقى من نسلك عدد قليل من بعد كثرتهم التي كانت قد صارت مثل نجوم السماء

BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r4.speaker: موسى
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r4.claim: Moses recalls God's plagues and signs against Egypt and Pharaoh, while saying God had not yet given Israel understanding, sight, or hearing.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r4.anchor: قد رأيتم ما صنع الله بأرض مصر بفرعون وجميع عبيده وكل شعبه والبلايا العظيمة التي رأت أعينكم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r5.speaker: موسى
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r5.claim: God sustained Israel through forty wilderness years: their clothes and sandals did not wear out, they ate no bread, and this was to teach them that He was their God.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r5.anchor: ودبركم في البرية أربعين سنة , لم تبل ثيابكم عليكم ولم تخلق خفافكم أيضا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r6.speaker: موسى
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r6.claim: Moses calls Israel to keep the Torah's commandments and complete all its works in obedience to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r6.anchor: فاحفظوا وصايا هذه التوارة واعلموا بها وأتموا جميع الأعمال في طاعة الله وأكملوها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r7.speaker: موسى
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r7.claim: The covenant warns that a man, woman, clan, or tribe might turn from worship of God to the gods of other peoples.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p143/r7.anchor: ولعل فيكم اليوم رجلا أو امرأة أو قبيلة أو سبطا يميل قبلة عن عبادة الله ربنا ويطلب عبادة آلهة تلك الشعوب

BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r1.claim: The cited covenant warning says those who abandon God’s covenant incur anger, curse, destruction, and exile; later generations identify the broken covenant as the cause.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r1.anchor: تركوا عهد الله إله آبائهم , فاشتد غضب الرب عن بلادهم بغضب وزجحر شديد ويبعدهم إلى أرض غريبه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r2.claim: The captivity that followed their punishment caused God to disperse them extensively across the earth into many separate groups.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r2.anchor: بسبب ما حصل لهم من السبي المترتب على العذاب بما لنا من العظمة تقطيعا كثيرا بأن أكثرنا تفريقهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r3.claim: Only a few lived in each town, leaving them without collective strength or the ability to defend themselves against oppression.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r3.anchor: فصار في كل بلدة قليل منهم ليست لهم شوكة ولا يدفعون عن أنفسهم ظلما

BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r4.claim: The righteous remained on their religion until its abrogating dispensation came, then followed it in obedience to the call of their own scripture.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r4.anchor: الذين ثبتوا على دينهم إلى أن جاء الناسخ له فتبعوه امتثالا لدعوة كتابهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r5.claim: Others fell below that standing, sometimes through wickedness and sometimes through disbelief.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r6.claim: God tested them with blessings and calamities in hope that desire for good or fear of harm would bring them back.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p144/r6.anchor: { بالحسنات } اي النعم { والسئات } اي النقم { لعلهم يرجعون } أي ليكون حالهم حال من يرجى رجوعه

DURR-FULL:v3p592/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p592/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p592/r3.claim: Mujāhid identifies the dispersed groups as Jews; the righteous are the People of the Book who became Muslims, while those below them are Jews.
DURR-FULL:v3p592/r3.anchor: {وقطعناهم في الأرض أمما} قال: يهود {منهم الصالحون} وهم مسلمة أهل الكتاب {ومنهم دون ذلك} قال: اليهود

DURR-FULL:v3p592/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p592/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p592/r4.claim: Mujāhid glosses the good things as ease and well-being, and the evil things as trial and punishment.
DURR-FULL:v3p592/r4.anchor: {وبلوناهم بالحسنات} قال: الرخاء والعافية {والسيئات} قال: البلاء والعقوبة

DURR-FULL:v3p592/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p592/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p592/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says umam means groups or factions; he cites Bishr b. Abī Ḥāzim's verse about Qays Ghaylān's groups as evidence for this sense.
DURR-FULL:v3p592/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قول الله {وقطعناهم في الأرض أمما} ما الأمم قال: الفرق وقال فيه بشر بن أبي حازم: من قيس غيلان

DURR-FULL:v3p592/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p592/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p592/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the blessings and hardships as fertility and drought.
DURR-FULL:v3p592/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وبلوناهم بالحسنات والسيئات} قال: بالخصب والجدب

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God spread the Jews throughout the earth, with no region lacking a group of them.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : وقطعناهم في الأرض امما هم اليهود بسطهم الله في الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God dispersed the Jews widely, placing people from them in every territory.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس وقطعناهم في الأرض امما منهم قال : مزقهم كل ممزق فجعل في كل كورة منهم اناس يعني اليهود

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r3.claim: Mujāhid says “communities” means Jews; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports the same.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد امما قال : يهود ، وروى عن سعيد بن جبير مثل ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r4.claim: Mujāhid says the righteous among them are the Muslims among the People of the Book.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : منهم الصالحون وهم مسلمو اهل الكتاب

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r5.speaker: سعيد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r5.claim: Saʿīd says the righteous among them are members of Muḥammad's community.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r5.anchor: عن سعيد قوله : منهم الصالحون قال : من امة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r6.claim: Mujāhid says those below the righteous are the Jews.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r6.anchor: من مجاهد ومنهم دون ذلك قال : اليهود

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r7.speaker: سعيد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r7.claim: Saʿīd says those below the righteous are those who did not believe in Muḥammad.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r7.anchor: عن سعيد قوله ومنهم دون ذلك قال : من لم يؤمن بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r8.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī says they were tested by prosperity but did not endure it patiently.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظى قال : ابتلوا بالرخاء فلم يصبروا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “the good things” as al-ḥaṣb (الحصب).
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس في قوله : وبلوناهم بالحسنات قال الحصب

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r10.claim: Mujāhid says “the good things” means prosperity and well-being.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1605/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : وبلوناهم بالحسنات قال : الرخاء والعافية

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “the bad things” as tribulation and punishment.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : والسيئات قال : البلاء والعقوبة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains “so that they might return” as “so that they might repent.”
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1606/r2.anchor: عن الحسن لعلهم يرجعون لعلهم يتوبون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r1.claim: The verse resumes the narrative of their circumstances; qattaʿnāhum can describe either blameworthy dispersal after unity or a praiseworthy division, depending on context, as in 7:160.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r1.anchor: فالتعويل على القرينة لا على لفظ التقطيع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r2.claim: “The earth” here is generic and means across the regions of the earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r2.anchor: فالمراد من الأرض الجنس أي في أقطار الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r3.claim: Umam is the plural of umma in the sense of a community or group.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r3.anchor: و { أمما } جمع أمة بمعنى الجماعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r4.claim: On the blameworthy reading, the verse refers to successive exiles: Assyrian capture of Israel and transfer to Babylon in 721 BCE, Babylonian capture of Judah and Jerusalem in 578 BCE, return in 530, then Roman expulsion under Titus in the early second century CE.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r4.anchor: ونقلهم إلى جبال انشور وأرض بابل سنة 721 قبل الميلاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r5.claim: Saying some were righteous indicates that dispersal included both the guilty and others; God gave the righteous honor among the nations where they settled, as the following trials show.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r5.anchor: بأن التفريق شمل المذنبين وغيرهم ، وأن الله جعل للصالحين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r6.claim: “Below that” includes everyone who fell short of righteousness, across varying degrees.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r6.anchor: وشمل قوله : { ومنهم دون ذلك } كل من لم يكن صالحا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r7.claim: The righteous kept Moses' law, affirmed later prophets, and believed Jesus; after Muhammad, only a few Jews such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and Mukhayriq remained righteous by believing in him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r7.anchor: و { الصالحون } هم المتمسكون بشريعة موسى والمصدقون للأنبياء المبعوثين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r8.claim: Dūna dhālika can be an adverb describing an omitted “group” understood from minhum; alternatively, min may be a noun meaning “some,” with minhum as subject and dūna as predicate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p157/r8.anchor: على الظرفية وصفا لمحذوف دل عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r1.claim: Another reported possibility places the division during the Babylonian kingdoms: among those living in Babylon were righteous people such as Daniel and others, as well as a less righteous group.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r1.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون الآية تشير إلى تفريقهم في الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r2.claim: The wording “some of them” suggests both groups were numerous.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r2.anchor: لأن التقسيم بمنهم مشعر بوفرة كلا الفريقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r3.claim: The tests through good and bad revealed differing responses: patience and gratitude, or distress and disbelief; the terms mean things that please or trouble.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r3.anchor: أي أظهرنا مختلف حال بني إسرائيل في الصبر والشكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r4.claim: On this reading, blessings and hardships detail the test and are acts of God distributed to the righteous and the rest.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا يكون الحسنات والسيئات تفصيلا للبلوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r5.claim: “Perhaps they will return” is an explanatory resumption: the hope is that they repent when recalling the periods of blessing and hardship or seeing the contrasting groups' fortunes.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r6.claim: Return here means repentance: turning back from breaking the covenant and disobedience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r6.anchor: والرجوع هنا الرجوع عن نقض العهد وعن العصيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r7.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr offers his own alternative: the division may continue the account of divine favors, like 7:160, and mean that God multiplied them and settled them throughout the promised Holy Land.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r7.anchor: عودا إلى أخبار المنن عليهم ، فيكون كالبناء على قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r8.claim: On this alternative, “the earth” means the promised land of Jerusalem; mentioning it here, unlike in 7:160, indicates that they inhabited all of it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r8.anchor: أرض القدس الموعودة لهم أي لكثرناهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r9.claim: Calling some righteous is a fair acknowledgment after describing their groups' aggression and refusal to listen to admonition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r9.anchor: إنصافا لهم بعد ذكر أحوال عدوان جماعاتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r10.claim: On the favorable reading, God alternately treated them with mercy and requited the deeds of their masses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p158/r10.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الله عاملهم مرة بالرحمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r1.claim: “We scattered them” means that God dispersed them throughout the earth.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r2.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits a group of commentators’ claim that no place on earth lacks a community of Jews.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r2.anchor: قال الطبري عن جماعة من المفسرين: ما في الأرض بقعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r3.claim: The people intended are apparently the Israelites after Solomon, when their kingdom ended.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r3.anchor: والظاهر في المشار إليهم في هذه الآية أنهم الذين بعد سليمان وقت زوال ملكهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r4.claim: The author places this period before Jesus, since after rejecting Jesus the Israelites had no righteous people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r4.anchor: والظاهر أنه قبل مدة عيسى عليه السلام لأنه لم يكن فيهم صالح بعد كفرهم بعيسى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r5.claim: Historical accounts about this period are inconsistent and confused.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r5.anchor: وفي التواريخ في هذا الفصل روايات مضطربة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r6.claim: If ṣalāḥ means faith, dūna dhālika means those other than believers, namely disbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r6.anchor: أن يدعها صلاح الإيمان ف دون بمعنى غير يراد بها الكفرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r7.claim: If ṣalāḥ means worship, goodness, and their implications of faith, dūna dhālika may include believers who fall short of that degree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r7.anchor: وإن أريد بالصلاح العبادة والخير وتوابع الإيمان ف دون ذلك يحتمل أن يكون في مؤمنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r9.claim: The good things are health, prosperity, and the like as people ordinarily regard them; the bad things are their opposites.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r9.anchor: وبالحسنات الصحة والرخاء ونحو هذا مما هو بحسب رأي ابن آدم ونظره،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r10.claim: “So that they might return” is phrased from the human observer’s perspective and means returning to obedience and repenting of sin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p471/r10.anchor: وقوله: لعلهم أي بحسب رأيكم لو شاهدتم ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses the phrase as dividing them into groups.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the dispersed people are the Jews, with a group of them in every country.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس هم اليهود ليس من بلد إلا وفيه منهم طائفة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r3.claim: Muqatil identifies them as the Children of Israel.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r4.claim: Another explanation is that their affairs became scattered and their unity divided.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r4.anchor: وقيل معناه شتات أمرهم وافتراق كلمتهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r5.claim: The righteous among them are those who believed in Jesus and Muhammad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r5.anchor: وهم المؤمنون بعيسى ومحمد عليهما السلام ﴿ ومنهم دون ذلك ﴾ وهم الكفار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r6.claim: Those below that rank are unbelievers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r6.anchor: وهم الكفار وقال ابن جرير إنما كانوا على هذه الصفة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r7.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r7.claim: Ibn Jarir says this division described them before Jesus was sent and before their later apostasy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r7.anchor: وقال ابن جرير إنما كانوا على هذه الصفة قبل أن يبعث عيسى وقبل ارتدادهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r8.anchor: أي اختبرناهم ﴿ بالحسنات ﴾ وهي الخير والخصب والعافية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r9.claim: The good experiences are prosperity, abundance, and well-being.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r9.anchor: وهي الخير والخصب والعافية ﴿ والسيئات ﴾ وهي الجدب والشر والشدائد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r10.claim: The bad experiences are drought, evil, and hardships.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r10.anchor: وهي الجدب والشر والشدائد فالحسنات والسيئات تحث على الطاعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r11.claim: Both blessings and afflictions urge obedience: blessings prompt seeking more and fearing their loss; afflictions prompt seeking relief and safety.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r11.anchor: فالحسنات والسيئات تحث على الطاعة أما النعم فطلب الازدياد منها وخوف زوالها والنقم فلكشفها والسلامة منها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p279/r12.claim: The purpose is that they might repent.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r1.claim: God dispersed them across the land as peoples, factions, and groups.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r1.anchor: يذكر تعالى أنه فرقهم في الأرض أمما، أي: طوائف وفرقا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r2.claim: They included both righteous people and others below that standard, like the jinn who say some among them are righteous and some otherwise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r2.anchor: كما قالت الجن: {وأنا منا الصالحون ومنا دون ذلك كنا طرائق قددا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r3.claim: God tested them with ease and hardship, hope and fear, well-being and affliction, so that they might return.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p498/r3.anchor: أي: اختبرناهم {بالحسنات والسيئات} أي: بالرخاء والشدة، والرغبة والرهبة، والعافية والبلاء،

JISHUMI:v4p2762/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2762/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2762/r6.claim: Umaman is the direct object of qattaʿnāhum.
JISHUMI:v4p2762/r6.anchor: أمما نصب ب (قطعناهم). وبلوناهم عطف على

JISHUMI:v4p2762/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2762/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2762/r7.claim: Balawnāhum is coordinated with qattaʿnāhum: God divided them into groups and tested them, with some righteous and others less so.
JISHUMI:v4p2762/r7.anchor: وبلوناهم عطف على (قطعناهم) تقديره: قطعناهم أمما وبلوناهم؛ فمنهم الصالح، ومنهم دون ذلك.

JISHUMI:v4p2762/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2762/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v4p2762/r8.claim: Abu Muslim connects the passage to the Israelites’ story: God had earlier informed them that Muhammad would be sent and would prevail over the Jews until the Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v4p2762/r8.anchor: قيل: إنه يتصل بقصة بني إسرائيل يعني أعلمكم الله فيما أنزل إليكم قديما أنه يبعث محمدا

JISHUMI:v4p2762/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2762/r9.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2762/r9.claim: Abu Ali instead treats the passage as a new address to the Prophet informing people of this matter.
JISHUMI:v4p2762/r9.anchor: وقيل: بل هو ابتداء كلام للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وإعلام الناس بذلك، عن أبي علي.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r1.claim: God dispersed the Israelites across the earth as separate peoples, so few lands lack a group of them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r1.anchor: وفرقناهم فيها ، فلا يكاد يخلوا بلد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r2.claim: The righteous are identified either as those among them who believed in Medina or as those living beyond China.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r2.anchor: الذين آمنوا منهم بالمدينة ، أو الذين وراء الصين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r3.claim: Those ‘below that’ are people lower than the righteous in standing: unbelievers and sinners.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r3.anchor: منهم ناس دون ذلك الوصف منحطون عنه ، وهم الكفرة والفسقة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r4.claim: دون ذلك is nominative as an adjective of an omitted noun, meaning ‘people lower than that’; the same construction appears in 37:164.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r5.claim: The good and bad things are blessings and afflictions by which God tested them.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p163#3/r6.claim: The aim is that they stop their wrongdoing and repent.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r1.claim: “We divided them” means God dispersed them into separate groups across the land.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r2.claim: Their dispersion is explained as further punishment, breaking mutual support, or distinguishing the righteous from wicked, explaining the next phrase.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r2.anchor: وفي تفريقهم فيها ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : زيادة في الانتقام منهم . والثاني : ليذهب تعاونهم . والثالث : ليتميز الصالح من المفسر لقوله تعالى : { منهم الصالحون ومنهم دون ذلك }

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r3.claim: Testing with good and evil may mean reward and punishment, blessings and afflictions, or fertile and barren years.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p273#2/r3.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : بالثواب والعقاب . والثاني : بالنعم والنقم . والثالث : بالخصب والجدب .

MUJAHID:v1p248#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p248#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p248#3/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the people dispersed across the land as the Jews.
MUJAHID:v1p248#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ وقطعناهم في الأرض ﴾ يعني اليهود

MUQATIL:7:167-170/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r3.claim: God dispersed the Children of Israel through the earth into groups.
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r3.anchor: { وقطعناهم } ، يعنى وفرقناهم { فى الأرض أمما } ، يعنى فرقا، يعنى بنى إسرائيل

MUQATIL:7:167-170/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r4.claim: The righteous among them are believers; those below that rank are unbelievers.
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r4.anchor: { منهم الصالحون } ، يعنى المؤمنين، { ومنهم دون ذلك } ، يعنى دون الصالحين، فهم الكفار

MUQATIL:7:167-170/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r5.claim: The good and bad trials are prosperity and hardship, intended to bring them back to repentance.
MUQATIL:7:167-170/r5.anchor: يقول: ابتليناهم بالخصب والشدة، { لعلهم } ، يعنى لكى { يرجعون } [آية: 168] إلى التوبة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r1.claim: God dispersed them throughout the earth, so no land was without a group of them.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r1.anchor: وفرقناهم فيها فلا تخلوا بلد من فرقة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r2.claim: The righteous may be those who believed in Medina or those beyond China.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ أمما منهم الصالحون ﴾ الذين آمنوا منهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r3.claim: Those below that standard are people beneath righteousness, namely wrongdoers.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r3.anchor: ومنهم ناس دون ذلك الوصف منحطون عنه وهم الفسقة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r4.claim: «Dūna dhālik» is nominative as an adjective of an omitted noun: some people below that standard.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r4.anchor: ومحل دون ذلك الرفع وهو صفة لموصوف محذوف أى ومنهم ناس منحطون عن الصلاح

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r5.claim: Good and bad things are blessings and afflictions, including abundance and drought.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p44#3/r6.claim: «So that they may return» means cease wrongdoing and repent.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r1.claim: God dispersed them across lands and fragmented their affairs so they would not unite.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r1.anchor: أي فرقناهم في البلاد. أراد به تشتيت أمرهم، فلم تجمع لهم كلمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r2.claim: The righteous are variously those who believed in Muhammad, those who did not alter religion and died before Mosaic law was abrogated, or those beyond China.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r2.anchor: والمراد من آمن بمحمد عليه السلام، ومن لم يبدل منهم ومات قبل نسخ شرع موسى. أو هم الذين وراء الصين

QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r3.claim: Al-salihin is nominative as subject; minhum dun dhalik is adverbial and accusative, and al-Nahhas knows no one who raises it; it means unbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r3.anchor: قال النحاس: ولا نعلم أحدا رفعه. والمراد الكفار منهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r5.claim: Good conditions are prosperity and well-being, while bad conditions are drought and hardship.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r5.anchor: { بالحسنات } أي بالخصب والعافية. { والسيئات } أي الجدب والشدائد.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:168/r6.claim: The trials are intended to bring them back from unbelief.

BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r1.speaker: اليافعي
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r1.claim: Al-Yafi‘i's verse advises withdrawing from people and taking God as companion, since human hearts resemble scorpions when examined.
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r1.anchor: تجدهم عقاربا كذا في "روض الرياحين" لليافعي.

BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r2.claim: God dispersed the Israelites across regions so none was free of them, completing the consequence of turning from truth and ensuring they could never gather strength again.
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r2.anchor: أي : فرقنا بني إسرائيل {في الأرض} وجعلنا كل فرقة منهم في قطر

BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r3.claim: أمما is a circumstantial accusative modifying قطعناهم, or a second object because the verb implies جعلناهم.
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r3.anchor: حال من مفعول قطعناهم أي : حال كونهم جماعات أو مفعول ثان لقطعنا

BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r4.speaker: author
