BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r4.claim: The righteous among them are the religiously observant adherents of Moses' religion.
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r4.anchor: وهم المتدينون بدين موسى {ومنهم دون ذالك}

BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r5.claim: The phrase expands to ومنهم ناس دون ذلك: an omitted noun meaning people below that level is the subject and منهم a fronted predicate.

BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r6.speaker: التفتازاني
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r6.claim: Al-Taftazani says grammarians parse such paired adverbials with the first as predicate and second as subject, supplying an omitted noun, though reversal is less apt in meaning.
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r6.anchor: قال التفتازاني : قد شاع في الاستعمال وقوع المبتدأ والخبر ظرفين واستمر النحاة على جعل الأول خبرا

BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, ذلك can function like plural أولئك and point to the righteous, since a singular demonstrative may be used for duals and plurals.
BURSEVI:v3p204#3/r7.anchor: وجوز بمعنى أولئك فالإشارة إلى الصالحين وقد ذكر النحويون أن اسم الإشارة المفرد

BURSEVI:v3p205/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p205/r1.claim: God hopes they will stop and turn from unbelief and disobedience; blessings encourage obedience and hardships warn against sin.
BURSEVI:v3p205/r1.anchor: {لعلهم يرجعون} ينتهون فيرجعون عما كانوا عليه من الكفر والمعاصي

BURSEVI:v3p205/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v3p205/r2.claim: Kashifi says they should have thanked for blessings but became arrogant, and been patient in hardship but insulted God, claiming He was poor and His hand bound; they failed the test.
BURSEVI:v3p205/r2.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ايشانرا درنعمت شكر بايست كرد بطر واستغنا ظاهر كردند

BURSEVI:v3p205/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p205/r3.claim: A Persian poem says the touchstone of experience exposes whoever has lied.
BURSEVI:v3p205/r3.anchor: خوش بود كر محك تجربه آيدبميان تاسيه روى شودهركه دروغش باشد

BURSEVI:v3p205/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p205/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p205/r4.claim: The Najmiyya reading treats blessings as good works and self-admiration, as with Iblis; misdeeds become occasions for remorse, repentance, fear, and reverence, as with Adam returning to God in 7:23.
BURSEVI:v3p205/r4.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {وبلوناهم بالحسنات} أي : بكثرة الطاعات ورؤيتها والعجب بها كما كان حال إبليس {والسيئات} أي : المعاصي

RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r1.claim: This phrase indicates that the earlier promise in 7:167 concerned the whole Jewish people, whom God dispersed widely.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r1.anchor: قوله : { ليبعثن عليهم } ( الأعراف : 167 ) المراد جملة اليهود

RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r2.claim: Their dispersion means scarcely any inhabited country lacks a Jewish community; this is the usual state of affairs.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r2.anchor: وظاهر ذلك أنه لا أرض مسكونة إلا ومنهم فيها أمة ، وهذا هو الغالب

RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r3.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r3.claim: One view identifies the righteous as people of Moses's time, when a community guided by truth existed among them.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r3.anchor: قيل المراد القوم الذين كانوا في زمن موسى عليه السلام لأنه كان فيهم أمة يهدون بالحق

RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid identify the righteous as those who lived to meet the Prophet Muhammad and believed him.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد : يريد الذين أدركوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وآمنوا به

RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r5.claim: The people 'below that' are those who remained Jewish, as distinct from the righteous group.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r5.anchor: أي ومنهم قوم دون ذلك ، والمراد من أقام على اليهودية

RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r6.speaker: قائل
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r6.claim: An objection proposes this means people who were righteous but less righteous than the first group, closer to the surface wording.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r6.anchor: فإن قيل : لم لا يجوز أن يكون قوله

RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r7.claim: Al-Razi answers that 'so that they might return' in 7:169 shows this means people who persisted in Judaism and left righteousness.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r7.anchor: قلنا : أن قوله بعد ذلك : { لعلهم يرجعون } يدل على أن المراد بذلك

RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r8.claim: Good things are blessings, fertility, and health; bad things are famine and hardships.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r8.anchor: وهي النعم والخصب والعافية ، والسيئات هي الجدب والشدائد

RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r9.speaker: أهل المعاني
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r9.claim: The scholars of meanings say prosperity and adversity prompt obedience: blessings encourage it and afflictions warn through fear.
RAZI-FULL:v15p36/r9.anchor: قال أهل المعاني : وكل واحد من الحسنات والسيئات يدعو إلى الطاعة
